messages:
maya: Quick note from onboarding: Node sampleapp logs behave oddly when X-Request-Id is sent. Some lines show tiny float timestamps and level becomes debug for no clear reason. Repro and snippets below. Anyone seen this?

kevin: hmm. paste the logger init + where you attach request log. looks like a monkeypatch/timing issue.

maya: Boot order: config -> logger -> OTEL auto-instrumentation -> express middleware. logger.js: `const pino = require('pino'); module.exports = pino({ level: process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'info', timestamp: pino.stdTimeFunctions.isoTime });` Middleware does `req.log = logger.child({ reqId: req.headers['x-request-id'] });`

sam: do you pretty-print or use multiple streams? otel can wrap console sometimes.

maya: no pretty-print. Removing OTEL init makes it stop. Changing init order didn't help. Removing `logger.child` also removes issue.

alex: can you paste raw lines?

maya: example from `ab` run:
`maya-service GET /api/foo 200 - 0.000234ms debug { reqId: 'abcd-1234' }`
`maya-service GET /api/foo 200 - 1617973.1234 info { reqId: 'efgh-5678' }`
Weird mix of tiny vs large float timestamps; level toggles.

kevin: sounds like two timestamp functions fighting or a child logger inheriting patched bindings lazily. which OTEL packages? node version?

maya: @opentelemetry/node 1.20.0, instrumentation-http 0.33.0, Node 18.16.0, pino 8.x.

sam: try a minimal repro without express: create parent logger, register OTEL instrumentations, create many children and log in a loop. See if it reproduces.

maya: reduced repro returns same behavior: with OTEL registered ~20% lines show tiny float + debug. Without OTEL, uniform.

alex: two likely causes: OTEL monkeypatches global time/console, or pino child is lazily binding a timestamp helper and race causes mixed behavior.

kevin: short-term workaround: stop using `logger.child` in middleware; call `logger.info({ reqId })` directly or create independent per-request logger instances. Also try pinning/downgrading OTEL.

maya: hacky patch: override `logger.child` to construct a fresh pino instance with same timestamp fn; reduced frequency but not ideal. Filed a repo PR with repro: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/88

ci-bot: Created INF-2026: "pino child logger + opentelemetry instrumentation causes inconsistent timestamps/level" https://tracker/redwood/INF-2026

maya: I'll update sampleapp docs with recommended logging pattern (avoid child loggers in middleware) and add a smoke check.

alex: agree - doc + onboarding checklist + link INF-2026. If infra sees it on prod, escalate.

kevin: I'll draft a short devex note and suggested code snippets.

maya: thanks all, updating PR now.
